content: Do not take olmesartan if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking olmesartan, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication can harm the fetus. Olmesartan is prescribed to treat high blood pressure, either alone or in combination with other medications. It belongs to a class of drugs called angiotensin II receptor antagonists, which work by blocking certain chemicals that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily. Olmesartan is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily, with or without food. To ensure consistent use, take it at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take olmesartan exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it, but not more than once every two weeks. While olmesartan helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure it. It may take up to two weeks to experience the full benefits. Continue taking olmesartan even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Olmesartan may also be used to treat heart failure. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. It may also be prescribed for other uses; ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking olmesartan, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially diuretics (water pills). Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart failure, kidney disease, or angioedema (a condition causing difficulty swallowing or breathing and painful swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs). Let your doctor know if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. Be aware that olmesartan may cause your blood pressure to drop too low, especially after the first dose. Your doctor may want you to take the first dose in their office to monitor your reaction. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Olmesartan may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience dizziness, especially if it is severe or persistent. Serious side effects are uncommon but require immediate medical attention. These include swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; and difficulty swallowing or breathing. Contact your doctor if you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store olmesartan in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the person has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include fainting, dizziness, blurred vision, upset stomach, and fast or slow heartbeat. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular blood pressure monitoring to assess your response to olmesartan. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
